## Verdict

**Dorado** costs least for a team of 18, at **$162 per month**. It is the only vendor whose minimum (10 seats) falls below the team size, so all 18 seats bill at the list rate of $9. Inkwell forces payment for 25 seats and Borealis for 50, pushing both well past their headline rates at this headcount.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $9 | 10 |
| Inkwell | $14 | 25 |
| Borealis | $19 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 18 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Dorado:** minimum 10 < 18, so 18 seats paid. 18 × $9 = **$162 per month**. Effective rate $9.00 per person.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 25 > 18, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $14 = **$350 per month**. Seven unused seats, worth $98. Effective rate $19.44 per person ($350 ÷ 18).
- **Borealis:** minimum 50 > 18, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $19 = **$950 per month**. Thirty-two unused seats, worth $608. Effective rate $52.78 per person ($950 ÷ 18).

Dorado is $188 per month cheaper than Inkwell and $788 per month cheaper than Borealis — $2,256 and $9,456 per year.

## Risks

Seat minimums, not per-seat rates, drive this result, so the gaps are size-sensitive. Inkwell's $350 is fixed until 25 people, at which point its effective rate drops to $14 against Dorado's $225 — Dorado still leads on list price at every size here. Borealis does not reach its $19 rate until 50 seats.

This is a price comparison only. The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits, or security posture, so the cheapest seat may not be a comparable product.

All figures assume monthly billing at list price as stated. Annual commitments, volume discounts, onboarding fees, and migration costs are not in the source and could reorder these totals. Confirm whether minimums are enforced at signup or persist if headcount falls.
